Human: Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Caro game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java Caro state-machine and deterministic-test contract:
- use freestyle Gomoku semantics on a square board: five or more contiguous stones wins immediately; WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1)
- the canonical Game API is exactly Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), and java.util.List<Move> getHistory(); Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false without mutation
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner
- undo returns false without mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn
- Board uses one empty-cell representation consistently; isEmpty and clearCell must agree with it, snapshot returns a deep copy, and getHistory/asReadOnly return unmodifiable copies or views
- Main.main must finish by normal method return after at most one concise print; System.exit, Runtime.getRuntime().exit/halt, infinite loops, input, GUI, and background threads are forbidden because MainTest invokes Main.main inside the Surefire JVM
- MainTest.java contains exactly three concise JUnit Jupiter tests and no invented sequences: (1) Main.main(new String[0]) returns normally; (2) the exact horizontal win sequence below; (3) the exact invalid-move, undo, and reset fixture below; vertical/diagonal/draw are implementation requirements but MUST NOT add long alternative test fixtures
- the sole win fixture is literally on one new Game(15): (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7); execute this sequence exactly once, assert all nine placeMove calls true, then status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, and history size 9; do not construct a second game to replay prefixes, do not directly call WinDetector from MainTest, and never assert that the ninth move or WinDetector at (7,7) is false; no tenth move is attempted except one terminal placeMove asserted false with no mutation
- the sole state fixture is literally: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true and changes turn to O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O/history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empty (1,1), empty history, and IN_PROGRESS; never expect O immediately after reset
- for architecture validation, the task document must literally preserve the compact sequence `(7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7)`, must say `exactly three` tests, and must mention both `placeMove(1,1)` and `placeMove(2,2)`; the phrase "nine consecutive X moves" or any test loop that lets X occupy every move is forbidden
- pom.xml must use Java 11, JUnit Jupiter test scope, and a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin; every class remains in the default package with no package declaration
- repeat the exact Game API, X-first/reset rule, toggle-only-while-in-progress rule, undo semantics, four-direction two-sided count, single nine-move win sequence, normal-return/no-System.exit rule, three-test limit, and literal state fixture in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague statements about alternation, wins, or reset are insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 38 functions or methods
- about 776 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- two-player board
- legal move validation
- alternating turns
- five-in-a-row detection in all directions
- draw state
- reset and move history

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.

- use freestyle Gomoku semantics on a square board: five or more contiguous stones wins immediately; WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1)

- undo returns false without mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn
- Board uses one empty-cell representation consistently; isEmpty and clearCell must agree with it, snapshot returns a deep copy, and getHistory/asReadOnly return unmodifiable copies or views

Tests are deterministic, offline, and headless; they exercise only the canonical Game API. No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.

Full API specification (explicit repetition):
- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().
- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.
- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.

Logic Analysis (explicit repetition):
- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).
- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.
- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.
- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.
- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).
- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.

Test Scope Plan (explicit repetition):
- Exactly three tests; no additional tests, no loops, deterministic, and offline.
- Test 1: Main.main returns normally without System.exit; at most one concise print.
- Test 2: The exact single nine-move horizontal win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) on a single new Game(15); assert all nine placeMove calls are true; final status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, history size 9; then perform exactly one terminal placeMove attempt and assert false with no mutation.
- Test 3: The state fixture: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true then turn O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O and history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empties (1,1), clears history, and IN_PROGRESS. This fixture explicitly mentions both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2).

- The single nine-move win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) and the literal state fixture mentioning both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2) appear in tests and inform implementations in Game, Board, and WinDetector.

Main is a minimal, headless entry that demonstrates a couple of safe moves and returns normally with at most one concise print. Tests are deterministic, offline, and headless; they exercise only the canonical Game API. No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.\\n\\nFull API specification (explicit repetition):\\n- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().\\n- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).\\n- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).\\n- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.\\n- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).\\n- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.\\n- WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) counts the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1). Five or more contiguous stones wins immediately (four-direction two-sided count).\\n\\nLogic Analysis (explicit repetition):\\n- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).\\n- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.\\n- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.\\n- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.\\n- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).\\n- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (explicit repetition):\\n- Exactly three tests; no additional tests, no loops, deterministic, and offline.\\n- Test 1: Main.main returns normally without System.exit; at most one concise print.\\n- Test 2: The exact single nine-move horizontal win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) on a single new Game(15); assert all nine placeMove calls are true; final status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, history size 9; then perform exactly one terminal placeMove attempt and assert false with no mutation.\\n- Test 3: The state fixture: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true then turn O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O and history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empties (1,1), clears history, and IN_PROGRESS. This fixture explicitly mentions both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2).\\n\\nShared Knowledge (explicit repetition for team alignment: Bob, Eve, Alex):\\n- Canonical Game API signatures and behaviors No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.\\n\\nFull API specification (explicit repetition):\\n- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().\\n- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).\\n- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).\\n- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.\\n- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).\\n- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.\\n- WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) counts the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1). Five or more contiguous stones wins immediately (four-direction two-sided count).\\n\\nLogic Analysis (explicit repetition):\\n- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).\\n- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.\\n- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.\\n- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.\\n\\nFull API specification (explicit repetition):\\n- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().\\n- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).\\n- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).\\n- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.\\n- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).\\n- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.\\n- WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) counts the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1). Five or more contiguous stones wins immediately (four-direction two-sided count).\\n\\nLogic Analysis (explicit repetition):\\n- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).\\n- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.\\n- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.\\n- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.\\n- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).\\n- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (explicit repetition):\\n- Exactly three tests; no additional tests, no loops, deterministic, and offline.\\n- Test 1: Main.main returns normally without System.exit; at most one concise print.\\n- Test 2: The exact single nine-move horizontal win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) on a single new Game(15); assert all nine placeMove calls are true; final status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, history size 9; then perform exactly one terminal placeMove attempt and assert false with no mutation.\\n- Test 3: The state fixture: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true then turn O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O and history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empties (1,1), clears history, and IN_PROGRESS. Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Caro game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java Caro state-machine and deterministic-test contract:
- use freestyle Gomoku semantics on a square board: five or more contiguous stones wins immediately; WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1)
- the canonical Game API is exactly Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), and java.util.List<Move> getHistory(); Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false without mutation
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner
- undo returns false without mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true

4) src/main/java/GameState.java (owner: Eve)

5) src/main/java/Board.java (owner: Alex)
   - Task: Implement Board with a square grid int size; backing 2D array of Player or null for empty-cell representation. Methods:

     - int getSize()
     - boolean isInBounds(int row, int col)
     - Player getCell(int row, int col)
     - boolean isEmpty(int row, int col): returns true iff getCell==null; this is the single empty-cell representation.
     - boolean setCell(int row, int col, Player p): set only if cell empty and in bounds; return true; otherwise false with no mutation (Game guards additional rules).

6) src/main/java/WinDetector.java (owner: Alex)
   - Task: Implement a pure utility class WinDetector with static boolean hasFiveInRow(Board b, int row, int col, Player p). The function must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly the four directions: (0,1) horizontal, (1,0) vertical, (1,1) diagonal down-right, (1,-1) diagonal up-right.      - public Game(int size)
     - public Board getBoard()
     - public Player getCurrentPlayer()
     - public GameState getState()
     - public boolean placeMove(int row, int col)
     - public boolean undo()
     - public void reset()
     - public java.util.List<Move> getHistory()

   - Allowed import direction: depends on Player, Move, Board, GameState, WinDetector.

   - Task: Runtime entry. Provide public class Main with public static void main(String[] args). - avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Main is a minimal, headless entry that demonstrates a couple of safe moves and returns normally with at most one concise print. Tests are deterministic, offline, and headless; they exercise only the canonical Game API. No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.

Full API specification (explicit repetition):
- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().
- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.
- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).

- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).
- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.
- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.
- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.
- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).
- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.

This fixture explicitly mentions both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2).

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve Maven protocol files exactly and keep runtime entry thin. Use Java 11, default package for all classes, and Maven Surefire configured for JUnit Jupiter. The core is decomposed into concrete domain entities (Player, Move, Board, GameState), a pure rule (WinDetector), and orchestration (Game). Main is a minimal, headless entry that demonstrates a couple of safe moves and returns normally with at most one concise print. Tests are deterministic, offline, and headless; they exercise only the canonical Game API. No GUI, no System.exit, no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter.

Full API specification (explicit repetition):
- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().
- Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X (X-first/reset rule).
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win via WinDetector.hasFiveInRow then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false with no mutation (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule and normal-return/no-System.exit rule).
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner.
- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.
- WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) counts the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1). Five or more contiguous stones wins immediately (four-direction two-sided count).

Logic Analysis (explicit repetition):
- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).
- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.
- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.
- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.
- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).
- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.

Test Scope Plan (explicit repetition):
- Exactly three tests; no additional tests, no loops, deterministic, and offline.
- Test 1: Main.main returns normally without System.exit; at most one concise print.
- Test 2: The exact single nine-move horizontal win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) on a single new Game(15); assert all nine placeMove calls are true; final status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, history size 9; then perform exactly one terminal placeMove attempt and assert false with no mutation.
- Test 3: The state fixture: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true then turn O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O and history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empties (1,1), clears history, and IN_PROGRESS. This fixture explicitly mentions both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2).

Shared Knowledge (explicit repetition for team alignment: Bob, Eve, Alex):
- Canonical Game API signatures and behaviors are fixed: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().

- Undo semantics and four-direction two-sided count in WinDetector are mandatory.
- The single nine-move win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) and the literal state fixture mentioning both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2) appear in tests and inform implementations in Game, Board, and WinDetector.

- use freestyle Gomoku semantics on a square board: five or more contiguous stones wins immediately; WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1)

Required domain behavior:
- two-player board
- legal move validation
- alternating turns
- five-in-a-row detection in all directions
- draw state
- reset and move history

- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix

- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC

- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Full API specification (explicit repetition):
- The canonical Game API is exactly: Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), java.util.List<Move> getHistory().

- undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true (undo semantics).
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn.

Logic Analysis (explicit repetition):
- Alternation occurs only while the game remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win, currentPlayer remains the winner (toggle-only-while-in-progress rule).
- Illegal moves (occupied or out-of-bounds) return false with no mutation; terminal state prevents further mutation; normal-return/no-System.exit rule is maintained across runtime and tests.
- Win detection strictly evaluates two-sided contiguous counts for four directions: (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) using the just-placed stone; five or more contiguous stones wins immediately.
- Undo semantics: removes last move, clears its cell, restores currentPlayer to that move's player, and sets state to IN_PROGRESS. Undo returns false with no mutation when history is empty.
- Reset semantics: fully clears board and history; sets currentPlayer to Player.X and state to IN_PROGRESS regardless of prior turn (X-first/reset rule).
- Sequence coverage targets the exact nine moves: (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) with Player.X winning horizontally and remaining the currentPlayer.

Test Scope Plan (explicit repetition):
- Exactly three tests; no additional tests, no loops, deterministic, and offline.
- Test 1: Main.main returns normally without System.exit; at most one concise print.
- Test 2: The exact single nine-move horizontal win sequence (7,3),(0,0),(7,4),(0,2),(7,5),(0,4),(7,6),(0,6),(7,7) on a single new Game(15); assert all nine placeMove calls are true; final status X_WON, winner Optional.of(Player.X), currentPlayer Player.X, history size 9; then perform exactly one terminal placeMove attempt and assert false with no mutation.
- Test 3: The state fixture: new Game(15) starts X; placeMove(1,1) is true then turn O; repeated placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(-1,0) are false and leave turn O and history size 1; placeMove(2,2) is true and changes turn to X; undo is true, makes (2,2) empty, restores turn O, leaves history size 1 and IN_PROGRESS; reset restores X, empties (1,1), clears history, and IN_PROGRESS. This fixture explicitly mentions both placeMove(1,1) and placeMove(2,2).

Project-specific Java Caro state-machine and deterministic-test contract:
- use freestyle Gomoku semantics on a square board: five or more contiguous stones wins immediately; WinDetector.hasFiveInRow(Board,int,int,Player) must count the just-played stone plus matching stones in both signs of exactly (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), and (1,-1)
- the canonical Game API is exactly Game(int size), Board getBoard(), Player getCurrentPlayer(), GameState getState(), boolean placeMove(int row,int col), boolean undo(), void reset(), and java.util.List<Move> getHistory(); Game(int size) rejects size<5 with IllegalArgumentException and every new or reset game starts with Player.X
- placeMove has no Player argument: while IN_PROGRESS it returns false without mutation for an out-of-bounds or occupied cell; otherwise it places currentPlayer, appends exactly one Move, evaluates win then draw, and advances to currentPlayer.next() only when the resulting state remains IN_PROGRESS; after a win currentPlayer therefore remains the winner, and every terminal call returns false without mutation
- GameState uses exactly Status.IN_PROGRESS, Status.DRAW, Status.X_WON, and Status.O_WON; GameState.won(Player.X) produces X_WON and winner X, GameState.won(Player.O) produces O_WON and winner O, while inProgress/draw have an empty winner
- undo returns false without mutation when history is empty; otherwise it removes exactly the latest move, clears that board cell, restores currentPlayer to the removed move's player, restores GameState.inProgress(), and returns true
- reset clears every board cell and the complete history, restores currentPlayer=Player.X and GameState.inProgress(); it must never derive the first player from the pre-reset current turn
- Board uses one empty-cell representation consistently; isEmpty and clearCell must agree with it, snapshot returns a deep copy, and getHistory/asReadOnly return unmodifiable copies or views
